newsitem.title: UK: Pru's Davies to head UK welfare plan - sources.
newsitem.headline: Pru's Davies to head UK welfare plan - sources.

text.p: Sir Peter Davies, chief executive of the British life insurance firm Prudential Corp Plc, has been chosen as head of Britain's new "welfare to work" programme, sources said on Wednesday.

The government's plan aims to create 250,000 jobs for young people who have been unemployed for at least six months. It will be funded by a so-called "windfall tax" on privatised utilities. Davies will not take a salary for his role and will continue in his position at the Prudential, they added.
On Tuesday Prime Minister Tony Blair promised the Labour government's budget, which is due on July 2, would focus on welfare-to-work.

Money raised through the windfall tax will provide job subsidies to employers willing to take on under 25-year-olds who have been out of work for more than six months, or to provide training, education or places on an environmental task force.
The announcement of Davies' appointment is expected to be made later on Wednesday. Prudential was not immediately available for comment.
